abstract: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. Supporting experiments examine acoustic feature selection, statistical pooling and Transformer patch configurations. The two-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved a mean macro-F1 of \textbf{(99.14 \textpm{} 0.32)\%} across five random seeds. The radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) achieved \textbf{98.83\%}, with a median end-to-end latency of 28.109~ms compared with 120.655~ms for the CNN. This favourable trade-off motivated RBF-SVM deployment on the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. It maintained the same classification performance with a median end-to-end latency of \textbf{349.09~ms} and a sustained throughput of \textbf{2.962 classifications/s}, or \textbf{14.8} times the rate required for consecutive five-second audio segments.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文用 ShipsEar 五秒音频比较六种分类器在树莓派 5 上的完整音频到预测流程，发现两层 CNN 准确最高而 RBF-SVM 只低 0.31 个百分点却快 4.29 倍，因而把 RBF-SVM 部署到 Zero 2 W 仍能跟上连续音频的速度。
originalTitle: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment
readerTitle: 在树莓派上直接听船：轻量水下船舶分类如何兼顾准确与延迟
